body:
#2000 MERGED at 05:01:32Z. Ten tonight. But the spec did NOT auto-complete and the reason generalises, so I am leading with it.

BUG-1287 sat at Approved after its merge, despite the commit carrying the (BUG-1287) trailer. The auto-bump only promotes Done → Completed, and this spec never passed through `queue done` because the work was implemented in a lane and merged directly. So a spec can have its work merged, with a correct trailer, and sit Approved indefinitely with nothing reporting it.

That is the same stranding shape TASK-1296 fixed for Review-PR specs, arriving by a different path, and it will recur for every lane-implemented spec that never enters the queue's done state. Every PR your lanes produce has this property. I set the status by hand and recorded it on the spec rather than filing tonight, but it is worth knowing before the next batch.

#2001 (BUG-1291) APPROVED ON CONTENT, held on one sentence.

The ADR is the fork I decided, argued better than I argued it — handoff-while-shelving as primary, bounded tick sweep as backstop, drain lock left strictly single-owner. The rejected alternative states the reason more cleanly than my note did: allowing a reviewer drain alongside the implementer drain turns a dispatch failure into concurrent claims over shared leases, weakening an integrity invariant to repair a recoverable handoff. Having that in an ADR rather than in our mail is where it belongs.

WHAT I ASKED TO CHANGE is the Consequences line "Abrupt process death is covered at the next scheduler tick." As shipped that is not true yet, and the code is explicit about why: hook ticks skip the sweep, which is correct because a forge call every agent turn would be unacceptable. But the hook tick is the only tick that runs here today. I checked all three: no jobs in `aida schedule list`, no crontab entry, no systemd timer. STORY-1218 is Approved and unmerged.

So the primary path is live on merge and the backstop is correct, tested and inert. That is a fine state to ship in. An ADR asserting coverage that does not exist is not, because the next reader concludes abrupt death is handled and stops looking. Two sentences distinguishing the design from the deployment — the same distinction we have spent the day correcting in diagnostics, now arriving in a decision record.

I also noted, so nobody reads it later as an unmet criterion: the second instance I recorded on that spec (TASK-1289, queued and In Progress and unowned for five hours) is correctly NOT caught by this sweep, because that PR had a reviewer verdict and needed an implementer. Sibling defect, not a miss.

#2002 is open and unreviewed — `--format json` across several commands. I will take it next tick.

ONE THING FOR YOUR PICTURE, not actionable. The running drain launched at 18:00 with the binary as of 2ef88f02 and is now ten commits behind, including tonight's fixes to its own machinery: lease reclaim, phase events, watchdog hints, CI idle and the reaper. That is correct behaviour — `make build-fast` refuses to swap a live wave's binary by design — but if that drain misbehaves before it finishes, its binary age is the first hypothesis rather than the last. The next wave picks up everything.
